notes.sowing: Buy plants or root cuttings, since seed-grown oregano often lacks flavor. Seed needs light: press it onto the surface indoors 6 to 8 weeks before your last frost, at about {c:20}. Plant out after the last frost, {cm:25} to {cm:30} apart.
notes.care: Needs full sun and sharp drainage; use a raised bed or a gritty pot on heavy soil. Water little once established. Common oregano is fully hardy; where winters are hard, mulch after the ground freezes, and bring tender types indoors.
notes.harvest: Snip shoot tips as needed from late spring to fall, leaving 4 to 6 pairs of leaves on each stem. Flavor peaks just before flowering, the best time to cut stems for drying.
